Accessibility

A site that works for everyone who needs it.

Energy decisions affect everyone, so this site is built to be usable with a keyboard, a screen reader, reduced motion preferences and small or heavily zoomed screens.

Note for the site owner

The business details used on this page are still template values from src/config/site.ts. Before launch, replace them and have this page reviewed against your actual business practices and legal obligations in your jurisdiction. This notice disappears once the placeholder details are updated.

How this site is built

Accessibility on this site is treated as part of the build, not a later patch. The specifics:

Structure and screen readers

  • Every page has one main heading and a logical heading order, with standard landmarks (header, navigation, main content, footer) so screen reader users can jump between regions.
  • A "skip to main content" link is the first thing keyboard users reach, letting them bypass the navigation on every page.
  • Photography carries descriptive alternative text; purely decorative graphics are hidden from assistive technology.

Keyboard operation

  • Everything interactive is a real link, button, input or control — nothing relies on a mouse-only click handler.
  • Focus is always visible, styled for both light and dark backgrounds.
  • The mobile navigation menu closes with the Escape key and returns focus to the button that opened it.
  • The image viewer on the solutions page behaves as a proper dialog: Escape closes it, arrow keys move between images, Tab stays inside it while open, and focus returns to the image you were viewing.
  • Frequently asked questions use expandable panels built from real buttons, with the expanded state announced; collapsed answers are excluded from the tab order.

Forms and errors

  • Every field has a visible label — placeholders are never the only label.
  • Hints and validation errors are programmatically associated with the fields they belong to, and invalid fields are marked so assistive technology reports them.
  • Required and optional fields are stated in words, not colour or an asterisk alone.

Motion, colour and zoom

  • Scroll and hover animations are reduced or removed when your system requests reduced motion.
  • Text colour combinations are chosen against WCAG AA contrast targets; the brightest accent colours are only used where the contrast against their background is sufficient.
  • Layouts are designed to reflow down to 320px-wide screens and to keep working when text is enlarged substantially.
  • There is no autoplaying audio or video, no flashing content, no CAPTCHAs and no time limits.

Honest limitations

  • This page describes how the site is designed and built. It has not yet been through an independent external audit; when one is carried out, its findings will be reflected here.
  • The typefaces are loaded from Google Fonts. If that request is blocked, the site falls back to system fonts and remains fully usable.
  • Links to third-party websites (for example, government rebate pages) are outside our control and may not meet the same standard.

Report a problem

If something on this site is difficult or impossible for you to use, we want to know — including which page it was and what assistive technology you were using. Use the contact page and we will follow up.

Changes to this page

This statement is reviewed as the site changes, and updated whenever the way the site works changes in a way that affects accessibility.
